newsitem.title: UK: UK unit trusts suffer MGAM effect in September [CORRECTED 12:36 GMT].
newsitem.headline: UK unit trusts suffer MGAM effect in September [CORRECTED 12:36 GMT].

text.p: Net retail sales of UK unit trusts declined to 205 million pounds in September from 347 million pounds in August as investors pulled out of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's troubled European investment funds, data released on Wednesday showed.

Figures published by the Association of Unit Trusts and Investment Funds (AUTIF) also showed a year-on-year decline in net retail sales of unit trusts for September, with sales of 218 million pounds recorded in the same month last year.

The figures give a preliminary view of how far confidence in unit trusts has been damaged following the three-day suspension of trading in three Deutsche Morgan Grenfell European funds on September 2.

Earlier this month Morgan Grenfell Asset Management dismissed four of its key managers in an attempt to restore its reputation from news of misvaluations in the three funds and the sacking of fund manager Peter Young.

London financiers have been concerned that, despite moves to staunch the losses via a cash injection from MGAM's parent Deutsche Bank, the confidence of small investors in the unit trust as an investment vehicle may have been hit.
"There does appear to have been a knock in confidence in the European sector more on the retail side, but I wouldn't expect outflows at that level to continue in the sector," an AUTIF official said.
Other sectors and vehicles benefited from the shift out of European unit trusts, the official said.

"There has been a certain amount of repositioning -- although there was in the European sector quite a high level of repurchases, at the same time a substantial amount of that money actually came back in, whether it was in other funds or other sectors," the official said, pointing to Personal Equity Plans (PEPs) in general and corporate bond PEPs in particular.
AUTIF's director general Philip Warland stressed that September's unit trust sales as a group were extremely strong.
"September's overall unit trust sales were remarkably strong, with net investment pushing up towards April's record figures," he said.
"Although net retail sales fell away this month, unit trust PEP sales remained consistent with the high levels reached throughout this year," he added.
Total net PEP sales for September came in at 327 million pounds compared with 307 million in August, while net sales of corporate bond PEPs rose to 76 million pounds from 62 million last month.
